findings.summary: build_features standardizes over the whole dataset before train_test_split, so test-set statistics leak into training features and the reported test AUC is optimistic.

Scaling statistics are not saved, so at inference build_features standardizes a single row or small batch against its own mean/std, giving NaN for single rows or differently scaled values, which corrupts production predictions (train/serve skew).
A zero-variance column (e.g. constant support_tickets) causes division by zero and fills the column with NaN, which makes LogisticRegression raise an error.
